title: 2026-11-18_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_b7c
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a compromised Linux host that appears to be infected with the Sofacy Fysbis backdoor. Your goal is to identify and analyze the malicious activities, understand the backdoor's behavior, and gather evidence for further remediation.
outcomes: Identify suspicious services and their associated ports.
Analyze systemd timers and services for persistence mechanisms.
Investigate lateral movement activities and unauthorized file transfers.

levels.title: Introduction

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity. Submit the exact service name as the answer.
levels.solution:
1. List all services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```
This command will display all services, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for running services:
```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running
```
Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

3. Check the status of the suspicious service:
```bash
systemctl status systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
This will provide details about the service, including its description and the command it executes.

4. Identify the service name:
From the status output, note the service name `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services, including inactive ones.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Filter for running services using `systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Check the status of the suspicious service with `systemctl status <service>`.

levels.title: Determine Network Port
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication. Submit the port number as the answer.
levels.solution:
1. Check the service configuration:
```bash
systemctl cat systemkernelservicedefender.service
```
This command will display the service unit file, which includes the `ExecStart` command.

2. Identify the port number:
In the `ExecStart` command, look for the port number specified as an argument to `ncat`. The port number is `80`.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` command in the service unit file.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Identify the port number specified as an argument to `ncat`.

levels.title: Identify System Information Collection Service
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity. Submit the exact timer name as the answer.
levels.solution:
1. List all timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --all
```
This command will display all timers, including inactive ones.

2. Filter for active timers:
```bash
systemctl list-timers --state=active
```
Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timer names.

3. Check the status of the suspicious timer:
```bash
systemctl status local-inventory.timer
```
This will provide details about the timer, including its description and the service it triggers.

4. Identify the timer name:
From the status output, note the timer name `local-inventory.timer`.
